summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory with mode 1777 (world rwx + sticky bit), owned by root:root. Sticky bit ensures only a file's owner (or root) can delete/rename it, while any user can write into the directory. Functionally verified with two test users (alice/bob): both could create files, neither could remove the other's file (Operation not permitted), each could remove their own. Test users were removed afterward. Completed the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol on node1: captured baseline boot_id and directory state, triggered a native reboot, polled through the outage until the node returned, confirmed a new boot_id (proving an actual restart, not just a service bounce), and re-verified /srv/drop's permissions and write functionality post-restart.
actions_performed: Confirmed root access on node1 (no sudo needed)
Created test users alice and bob
alice created and wrote a file in /srv/drop
bob's attempt to rm alice's file failed with 'Operation not permitted' (exit 1)
bob successfully created his own file in /srv/drop (exit 0)
alice successfully removed her own file (exit 0)
bob successfully removed his own file (exit 0)
Deleted alice and bob test accounts; confirmed removal via /etc/passwd and /etc/group grep
Captured baseline boot_id and directory state before restart
Triggered node1 reboot via backgrounded 'sleep 2; reboot' so acknowledgement returned before disconnection
Polled node1 through connection resets/timeouts until it came back online
Confirmed new boot_id and new uptime -s timestamp, proving the node actually restarted
Ran a post-restart write probe as user 'nobody' to confirm the directory remains writable, then cleaned up the probe file

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created with correct permissions (shared writable, sticky bit for owner-only delete)
evidence.summary: mkdir + chmod 1777 /srv/drop; stat confirms mode 1777, owner root:root

evidence.requirement: Functional proof: any user can write, only the file owner can delete their own file
evidence.summary: Created alice/bob test users; alice wrote a file; bob's rm of alice's file failed with 'Operation not permitted' while bob could still create his own file; alice removed her own file successfully; bob removed his own file successfully; test users cleaned up

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline before restart (boot identity + /srv/drop state)
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id af123507-55d4-4e55-af64-0195b1b7031b, uptime -s, and /srv/drop mode/contents prior to reboot
Backgrounded 'sleep 2; reboot' command returned its scheduling acknowledgement (pid=2854) immediately, before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node actually restarted (changed boot identity), not just a service bounce
evidence.summary: Polling sequence shows connection resets/timeouts during the reboot window, then a successful reconnect with a new boot_id (712a75dc-1423-4822-987c-f434e1a704ac) and new uptime -s (07:55:34), differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving a genuine restart

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery verification: /srv/drop config and functionality intact
evidence.summary: Post-restart stat shows /srv/drop still 1777 root:root; write probe by user 'nobody' succeeded and was cleaned up, confirming the shared writable/sticky directory survived the reboot
